line: You don’t know what you started, I pop a Perc’, go retarded
vault_lines: You don't know what you started, I pop a Perc', go retarded
meaning:
Traditionally, the term “retarded” was a controversial way of referring to an intellectually disabled person, however, the term “going retarded” has been colloquially used to compare the behavior of someone who has consumed enough drugs or alcohol to the point where they are acting similar to a mentally-retarded person.

Commonly abbreviated as “Percs,” Percocets are a combination of the opioid oxycodone with acetaminophen, used to treat moderate to severe short-term pain. When used to be consumed recreationally, they give the user a warm, euphoric feeling.

Pop used a similar line twice on “Invincible,” the opening track from his 2020 mixtape Meet the Woo 2, where he rapped:

I pop a Perc', go retarded, wait

line: I just caught a case, but I thank God it ain’t a RICO
vault_lines: I just caught a case, but I thank God it ain't a RICO
meaning:
Here Kodak might be referencing the RICO case in Orange County, where fellow Florida rappers (9lokkNine and Hotboii) and 32 others have been arrested on racketeering or drug trafficking.

More information on “Operation X-Force” can be read in an article by Complex.

The RICO Act is federal legislation which is used by prosecutors against various criminal organizations (e.g. the Mafia or street gangs). Many states have also legislated their own RICO Acts mirroring the federal law with variations, in Florida the law defines a criminal gang under 874 as an “enterprise”.

For RICO to be used against a person, prosecutors have to prove there has been a pattern of racketeering activity. The federal law defines 35 crimes as part of racketeering activity. To prove a pattern of activity requires at least two illegal acts within the last ten years, providing these are linked to an enterprise. Those found guilty of racketeering can be fined up to $25,000 and sentenced to 20 years in prison per racketeering count.

These cases are virtually unbeatable and it can charge lots of members of organized crime, who were not involved in the crime that made the feds or state investigate, to begin with. This is why Kodak thanks God it is not a RICO case he has ‘caught’ because his alleged affiliation with the Zoe Pound Gang or ZMF means he could easily be prosecuted due to his prior convictions.

meaning:
Exotic, or exotic weed, is a slang term for high-potency cannabis popular with street culture and rap music. It is also known as “zaza.” (Leafly)

Just as a tiger is exotic in America but not India, the label of exotic cannabis depends on the location and audience. To a newbie, almost anything with a high THC count and colorful trichome crystals will feel exotic. But the term does not traditionally describe familiar favorites like OG Kush, Sour Diesel or Jack Herer.

The name suggests origins in the tropics or Middle East, but for many it is nothing more than a marketing tool used to classify ambiguous but potent strains whose true genealogy is unknown to the dealer.

A supplier offering an exotic strain could have anything from a fruity sativa to a dark purple indica, but the general standard for the name is a top-shelf strain that is both rare for the region and has extremely noticeable effects. (Leafly)

Depending on where you’re at and the weed available, it could be worth the flight out to get something proper

“Shoot for the stars, aim for the moon” was a motto that Pop Smoke lived by, even being the planned name of his third album which was released posthumously.

Pop Smoke had plans to use his success to open doors for children that have limited access to educational resources. He had started reaching out to educators and institutions to set up a way to donate computers.

On January 22, 2020, Pop Smoke uploaded a video skit to Instagram revealing the release date for “Meet The Woo 2”. In the skit, he also announced his plans to open the Shoot for the Stars Foundation, donating $100,000 on the spot and getting Steven Victor to put in $250k. He then challenged Swizz Beatz to also pitch in.

Even though his untimely demise meant he never got to fully realize this vision, those around Pop made sure to continue his work. In June 2020, his family officially announced the Shoot for the Stars Foundation, a charitable organization to keep Bashar’s dream of supporting the youth in underprivileged areas alive.

Audrey Jackson, Pop Smoke’s mother, gave the following statement:

Bashar was in the process of becoming.  I have heard it said that African-American males are not allowed the mistakes of youth that young men of European ancestry are. He seemed to have identified a foundation formed by his spiritual upbringing and the streets.
This forum is the beginning of creating sacred space for young people to come together and start the conversation around the shift that they bring to the global stage.

These lines interpolate Pop’s viral 2019 drill hit “Dior,” specifically the climax of the track’s only verse:

Tell my shooters call me FaceTime
For all the times we had to face time
Free D-Nice, he doin' state time
If you need the glizzy, you could take mine

Although these lines are a callback to Pop Smoke’s earlier music, the lyrics are very much grounded in reality. In January of 2020, Pop Smoke had made away with a Rolls-Royce Wraith after it was rented to him for a one-day music video shoot. The owner discovered the car had been driven across state lines not long before the rapper was arrested and charged with its theft. Pop also graduated high school while wearing an ankle monitor resulting from a weapons charge. His troubled childhood included transferring to at least nine different schools to combat gun-related incidents. It’s clear that when facing consequences for crimes, Pop Smoke was never one to let up.

It’s always been strife, even if there were bundles of cash stowed away somewhere safe in his house. When he was 16 and beginning to earn money for himself independently, he purchased his first car, a Pepsi-blue beamer. Prior to this, life was dramatically different. ​“Shit was hard,” Pop Smoke says matter-of-factly, preferring not to divulge too much about his past.

—The Face, December 3, 2019.

These lines also mention a close friend of Pop Smoke, D-Nice. You can watch his reaction to Pop name-dropping him on “Dior” when he was released from state prison on October 3, 2020 below:
